channel.title: FortiGuard Labs | FortiGuard Center - IR Advisories
channel.description: The following is a list of advisories for issues resolved in Fortinet products. The resolution of such issues is coordinated by the Fortinet Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT), a dedicated, global team that manages the receipt, investigation, and public reporting of information about security vulnerabilities and issues related to Fortinet products and services.

item.title: Allocation of resources without limits or throttling in fastapi
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 7.5

An Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability [CWE-770] in FortiAuthenticator may allow an unauthenticated attacker to exhaust system resources, potentially resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

Revised on 2026-11-10 00:00:00

item.title: Arbitrary file write and delete in JSON API
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 7.3

An improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability [CWE-22] in FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer API may allow an authenticated attacker whose profile only has read permission to write and delete files from the underlying filesystem via crafted HTTP or HTTPs requests.

Revised on 2026-11-10 00:00:00

item.title: Authentication bypass
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.0

A Use of Hard-coded Password [CWE-259] vulnerability in FortiAuthenticator may allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass credential validation in certain circumstances outside of the attacker's control and gain unauthorized access.

Revised on 2026-11-10 00:00:00

item.title: Authentication bypass by primary weakness
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.3

An Authentication Bypass by Primary Weakness vulnerability [cwe-305] in FortiOS and FortiSASE ospf daemon may allow an unauthenticated attacker to broadcast LSA via specially crafted request

item.title: Authentication bypass by spoofing
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 8.2

An authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability (CWE-290) in FortiAnalyzer, FortiAnalyzer Cloud, FortiAnalyzer-BigData, FortiManager, FortiManager Cloud, FortiSASE-Sovereign fortilogd may allow an attacker to disrupt the HA state.

item.title: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key
item.description:

An Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability [CWE-639] in FortiMail may allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to take over an arbitrary IBE recipient account via crafted HTTP requests.

item.title: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key

item.title: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key

An Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability [CWE-639] in FortiMail may allow an authenticated remote attacker to delete arbitrary directories as root, or to access or delete other users' calendar and mailbox data across tenant domains, via crafted HTTP requests to the webmail and administrative interfaces.

item.title: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key

item.title: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in GUI

item.title: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in dmserver

item.title: Broken Access Control in Two-Factor-Authentication
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 5.9

An Improper Authentication vulnerability [CWE-287] in the FortiOS Remote Radius Type Admin Two-Factor (TFA) Authentication may allow a remote authenticated attacker with at least read-only permission to log in to the FortiOS GUI with an invalid token after entering a valid username and password, in scenarios where the RADIUS server returns an additional "Access-Challenge" response following an invalid TFA token.

Revised on 2026-11-10 00:00:00

item.title: FGFM elevation before registration password is verified
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.0

An improper authorization vulnerability in FortiManager FGFM may allow an unauthenticated attacker that can reach the FGFM port to execute code or commands via crafted FGFM packets.

Revised on 2026-11-10 00:00:00

item.title: Heap-based buffer overflow
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 7.2

A Heap-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability [CWE-122] in FortiManager, FortiManager Cloud, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAnalyzer Cloud may allow an authenticated administrator to execute unauthorized code or commands or cause a denial of service via specially crafted JSON-RPC requests.
